entries.08b0eb170c91db3b: In October 2014 it moved to a holding company structure and changed its company name from Dainippon Screen Mfg. Co., Ltd. to SCREEN Holdings Co., Ltd. At the same time, it had SCREEN Semiconductor Solutions Co., Ltd. succeed to the semiconductor production equipment business, and in November of the following month it had SCREEN Graphic and Precision Solutions Co., Ltd. succeed to the printing-related equipment and printed circuit board-related equipment businesses, and SCREEN Finetech Solutions Co., Ltd. succeed to the FPD equipment business and other equipment-related businesses. In April 2017 it had SCREEN PE Solutions Co., Ltd. succeed to the printed circuit board-related equipment business from the former, and the remaining company changed its company name to SCREEN Graphic Solutions Co., Ltd. As a forerunner of the spin-offs, in July 2002 it split off the domestic sales division for printing-related equipment and established Media Technology Japan Co., Ltd. (now SCREEN GP Japan Co., Ltd.).
entries.09e3ebe96f224ca1: Operating profit in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥122,522 million, down 9.7% from the previous fiscal year. The company explains that this was due to an increase in fixed costs such as research and development expenses and personnel expenses for growth, and a decrease in net sales. Ordinary profit was ¥124,323 million, down 10.1%, and net profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥92,003 million, down 7.5%. Segment profit was SPE122,707 million yen, FT8,605 million yen, GA3,602 million yen, PE383 million yen, and others -¥2,435 million. Care is needed here. The total profit of the 4 reporting segments, ¥135,298 million, does not agree with consolidated operating profit of ¥122,522 million. The adjustment of -¥10,340 million is, as Note 2 of the annual securities report states, “profit and loss of the company not allocated to business segments, etc.,” that is, the expenses of the holding company itself. Segment figures cannot be added together to obtain operating profit.

entries.5a660bc9de2e72a1: The company explains its core technologies as "surface and interface control technology" and "image processing technology," and the "system integration technology" that links them. Surface and interface control technology leads to cleaning equipment that removes fine contamination from the surface of semiconductor wafers, and image processing technology leads to printing systems and direct imaging systems that draw patterns directly onto substrates. The annual securities report states "the cleaning field, in which the group boasts the top share," and cleaning is this company's strong field. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, it developed the direct imaging exposure system "DW-3100," which it describes as having the world's highest level of resolution, for the advanced semiconductor packaging market, concluded an additional contract with IBM for development of next-generation cleaning processes in the advanced device field, and is also collaborating with overseas research institutions such as imec (Interuniversity Microelectronics Centre).

entries.a14fe1406b0dae4d: It makes equipment, delivers it to factories, and also earns revenue from maintenance and parts afterwards. SCREEN Holdings Co., Ltd. itself does not make equipment, and, as the [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states, 'under a holding company structure, it places operating companies by product and service, and each operating company formulates comprehensive strategies in Japan and overseas for the products and services it handles and develops business activities.' The 4 reportable [[term:segment|segments]] are those operating companies themselves: the semiconductor production equipment business (SPE) is SCREEN Semiconductor Solutions Co., Ltd., the graphic arts equipment business (GA) is SCREEN Graphic Solutions Co., Ltd., the display production equipment and film deposition equipment business (FT) is SCREEN Finetech Solutions Co., Ltd., and the printed circuit board-related equipment business (PE) is SCREEN PE Solutions Co., Ltd. Sales are heavily skewed toward SPE, and of revenue from external customers of ¥605,748 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026, ¥485,344 million is from SPE. Customers are also skewed, and the only 1 customer named by the annual securities report is Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, Ltd., with revenue of ¥88,507 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026, or 14.6% of total sales results. The decrease in sales of equipment for [[term:foundry|foundries]], which undertake the production of semiconductors, is also cited as a reason for the decrease in revenue in this year. By region, China at ¥232,534 million (38.4%) and Taiwan at ¥135,987 million (22.4%) together exceed 6 tenths, while Japan is limited to ¥85,639 million (14.1%).

entries.fc0f9017efe6642f: On October 11, 1943, Dainippon Screen Mfg. Co., Ltd. was established with capital of ¥130,000 and its head office was placed in Kyoto City. From March 1946 it began production of photographic platemaking machinery such as cameras, arc lamps and printing-down frames, and started out as a comprehensive manufacturer of photographic platemaking equipment. In June 1953 it acquired the Horikawa Plant, which is the current head office location. Its shares were listed on the Second Section of the Osaka Securities Exchange in May 1962 and on the Second Section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange in October 1967, were redesignated to the First Section of both exchanges in August 1970, and moved to the Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange in the market segment revision in April 2022.
